# Class exercise - the questions (written by C:/DE10_solutions/class_exercise/gen.py, do not edit).
# [Qnn] NAME | title | npub n [| steps n];  B: board;  Pk: printed for login numbers with pub = k;
# with steps: Sk: the screen of step k (step 0 = login, in run.ps1);  without: L: question, F: answer format

[Q01] GATE | Which gate is hidden in the board? | npub 1 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8 (HEX3, HEX2).  Y = LEDG0 (green).  Your answer goes on SW3..SW0.
S1: GOAL: meet the board. A gate is hidden in it: inputs A = SW9, B = SW8, output Y = LEDG0.
S1: Put A B = 0 0 (SW9 and SW8 down). Is the green light LEDG0 on?
S1: ANSWER: SW0 up if LEDG0 is on, SW0 down if it is off.
S2: GOAL: the whole truth table of the gate.
S2: Try A B = 00, 01, 10, 11 (SW9 SW8) and write Y for each row.
S2: ANSWER: SW0 = Y at 00,  SW1 = Y at 01,  SW2 = Y at 10,  SW3 = Y at 11.
S3: GOAL: name the gate. Compare your truth table with what each gate does.
S3: ANSWER - first put SW3 SW2 SW1 SW0 all DOWN, then raise only the switches of your gate:
S3:    AND = (all down)    OR = SW0    XOR = SW1    NAND = SW1 + SW0    NOR = SW2    XNOR = SW2 + SW0

[Q02] SIGMA | Minterms and maxterms of a hidden F | npub 1 | steps 6 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  F = LEDG0 (green).  Your answer goes on SW3..SW0.
S1: GOAL: meet F. It has three inputs: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7. F = LEDG0.
S1: Put A B C = 0 0 0 (SW9, SW8, SW7 down). Is LEDG0 on?
S1: ANSWER: SW0 up if LEDG0 is on, SW0 down if it is off.
S2: GOAL: the first half of the truth table - the 4 rows where A = 0. Keep SW9 DOWN.
S2: 1. Set SW8 SW7 like this, and write down LEDG0 (on = 1) for each row:
S2:       row 000: SW8 down, SW7 down      row 001: SW8 down, SW7 up
S2:       row 010: SW8 up,   SW7 down      row 011: SW8 up,   SW7 up
S2: 2. Copy the 4 lights to the right switches (up = 1):
S2: ANSWER: SW0 = row 000,  SW1 = row 001,  SW2 = row 010,  SW3 = row 011.
S3: GOAL: the second half - the 4 rows where A = 1. Keep SW9 UP.
S3: 1. Set SW8 SW7 like this, and write down LEDG0 (on = 1) for each row:
S3:       row 100: SW8 down, SW7 down      row 101: SW8 down, SW7 up
S3:       row 110: SW8 up,   SW7 down      row 111: SW8 up,   SW7 up
S3: 2. Copy the 4 lights to the right switches (up = 1):
S3: ANSWER: SW0 = row 100,  SW1 = row 101,  SW2 = row 110,  SW3 = row 111.
S4: GOAL: minterms. A row where F = 1 is a MINTERM: F = SIGMA(those row numbers).
S4: Count the rows of your table where F = 1.
S4: ANSWER: the number on the switches:   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S5: GOAL: maxterms. A row where F = 0 is a MAXTERM: F = PI(those row numbers).
S5: Count the rows of your table where F = 0.
S5: ANSWER: the number on the switches:   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0

[Q03] TERMS | Which light is a minterm, which a maxterm? | npub 1 | steps 5 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  4 terms = LEDG3..LEDG0 (green).  Your answer goes on SW3..SW0.
S1: GOAL: meet the 4 green lights. Each one is a TERM of A B C, like  A B'  or  A + C.
S1: Put A B C = 1 1 1 (SW9, SW8, SW7 up).
S1: ANSWER: copy the lights - SWi up if LEDGi is on (SW3..SW0).
S2: GOAL: ONE table of all 4 lights. Copy it to paper, go over the 8 rows once (0 = down, 1 = up),
S2: and mark the lights that are on in each row:
S2:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    LEDG3  LEDG2  LEDG1  LEDG0
S2:    0 0 0
S2:    0 0 1
S2:    0 1 0
S2:    0 1 1
S2:    1 0 0
S2:    1 0 1
S2:    1 1 0
S2:    1 1 1
S2: ANSWER: how many 1s in the LEDG0 column?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S3: GOAL: the MINTERM - all three letters ANDed, like  A B' C. It is ON in only ONE row.
S3: In your table, find the column with a single 1.
S3: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for that light (LEDGi).
S4: GOAL: the MAXTERM - all three letters ORed, like  A + B' + C. It is OFF in only ONE row.
S4: In your table, find the column with a single 0.
S4: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for that light (LEDGi).

[Q04] MATTER | Which input does not matter? | npub 1 | steps 5 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  F = LEDG0 (green).  Your answer goes on SW3..SW0.
S1: GOAL: the truth table of F. Copy it to paper, go over the 8 rows once (0 = down, 1 = up),
S1: and write F (LEDG0 on = 1) in each row:
S1:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    F
S1:    0 0 0
S1:    0 0 1
S1:    0 1 0
S1:    0 1 1
S1:    1 0 0
S1:    1 0 1
S1:    1 1 0
S1:    1 1 1
S1: ANSWER: how many 1s in the F column?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S2: GOAL: does A matter? Look at pairs of rows that differ ONLY in A (the first digit):
S2:    000 - 100      001 - 101      010 - 110      011 - 111
S2: If F is different in at least one pair, A matters.
S2: ANSWER: SW0 up if A matters, SW0 down if F is the same in all 4 pairs.
S3: GOAL: does B matter? Pairs that differ ONLY in B (the middle digit):
S3:    000 - 010      001 - 011      100 - 110      101 - 111
S3: ANSWER: SW0 up if B matters, SW0 down if F is the same in all 4 pairs.
S4: GOAL: one input never changes F - find it. (Check C too: pairs 000-001, 010-011, 100-101, 110-111.)
S4: ANSWER: raise ONE switch for the input that does NOT matter:   A = SW2    B = SW1    C = SW0

[Q05] SIGMA4 | Minterms and maxterms - four inputs | npub 1 | steps 7 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7, D = SW6 (HEX3..HEX0).  F = LEDG0 (green).  Answer on SW3..SW0.
S1: WHAT YOU DO: look at the green light LEDG0 for 4 positions of the switches, and write on/off.
S1: (16 positions in all - this is round 1 of 4.)
S1: 1. Put SW9 DOWN and SW8 DOWN. Do not touch them in this round.
S1: 2. SW7 down, SW6 down  - is the green light on?   write: position 1 = on / off
S1: 3. SW7 down, SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 2
S1: 4. SW7 UP,   SW6 down  - is it on?                position 3
S1: 5. SW7 UP,   SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 4
S1: ANSWER: for every position that was ON, raise one switch:
S1:    position 1 -> SW0      position 2 -> SW1      position 3 -> SW2      position 4 -> SW3
S2: ROUND 2 of 4 - the same as round 1, only SW9 and SW8 are different.
S2: 1. Put SW9 DOWN and SW8 UP. Do not touch them in this round.
S2: 2. SW7 down, SW6 down  - is the green light on?   write: position 1 = on / off
S2: 3. SW7 down, SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 2
S2: 4. SW7 UP,   SW6 down  - is it on?                position 3
S2: 5. SW7 UP,   SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 4
S2: ANSWER: for every position that was ON, raise one switch:
S2:    position 1 -> SW0      position 2 -> SW1      position 3 -> SW2      position 4 -> SW3
S3: ROUND 3 of 4 - the same as round 1, only SW9 and SW8 are different.
S3: 1. Put SW9 UP and SW8 DOWN. Do not touch them in this round.
S3: 2. SW7 down, SW6 down  - is the green light on?   write: position 1 = on / off
S3: 3. SW7 down, SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 2
S3: 4. SW7 UP,   SW6 down  - is it on?                position 3
S3: 5. SW7 UP,   SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 4
S3: ANSWER: for every position that was ON, raise one switch:
S3:    position 1 -> SW0      position 2 -> SW1      position 3 -> SW2      position 4 -> SW3
S4: ROUND 4 of 4 - the same as round 1, only SW9 and SW8 are different.
S4: 1. Put SW9 UP and SW8 UP. Do not touch them in this round.
S4: 2. SW7 down, SW6 down  - is the green light on?   write: position 1 = on / off
S4: 3. SW7 down, SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 2
S4: 4. SW7 UP,   SW6 down  - is it on?                position 3
S4: 5. SW7 UP,   SW6 UP    - is it on?                position 4
S4: ANSWER: for every position that was ON, raise one switch:
S4:    position 1 -> SW0      position 2 -> SW1      position 3 -> SW2      position 4 -> SW3
S5: HOW MANY TIMES WAS THE LIGHT ON? Count the ON positions you wrote in rounds 1-4 (16 positions in all).
S5: (A position where F is on is called a MINTERM.)
S5: ANSWER: put that number on the switches:
S5:    1 = SW0          2 = SW1          3 = SW1+SW0       4 = SW2           5 = SW2+SW0       6 = SW2+SW1
S5:    7 = SW2+SW1+SW0  8 = SW3          9 = SW3+SW0      10 = SW3+SW1      11 = SW3+SW1+SW0  12 = SW3+SW2
S6: HOW MANY TIMES WAS THE LIGHT OFF? That is 16 minus your answer before.
S6: (A position where F is off is called a MAXTERM.)
S6: ANSWER: put that number on the switches:
S6:    1 = SW0          2 = SW1          3 = SW1+SW0       4 = SW2           5 = SW2+SW0       6 = SW2+SW1
S6:    7 = SW2+SW1+SW0  8 = SW3          9 = SW3+SW0      10 = SW3+SW1      11 = SW3+SW1+SW0  12 = SW3+SW2

[Q06] THEOREMS | Perfect induction: which statements are true? | npub 4 | steps 4 | flat
B: Statement number = SW9 SW8 (HEX3).  A = SW7, B = SW6 (HEX1 HEX0).  LEFT = LEDG1, RIGHT = LEDG0.  Answer on SW3..SW0.
B: The board holds 4 statements LEFT = RIGHT, in a hidden order:   A + AB = A     A + A'B = A + B     (AB)' = A' + B'     (A + B)' = A' + B'
P0: Your statement for the last step:  A + AB = A
P1: Your statement for the last step:  A + A'B = A + B
P2: Your statement for the last step:  (AB)' = A' + B'
P3: Your statement for the last step:  (A + B)' = A' + B'
S1: GOAL: is statement 0 true?  SW9, SW8 down = statement 0.  LEDG1 = its LEFT side, LEDG0 = its RIGHT side.
S1: Set SW7 SW6 = down down,  down up,  up down,  up up.
S1: In each one: are LEDG1 and LEDG0 the SAME (both on or both off)?
S1: ANSWER: SW0 up if they were the same in all 4.  SW0 down if they were different even once.
S2: GOAL: the same check as step 1, for all 4 statements. Copy this table to paper:
S2:    statement   SW9 SW8      same in all 4?
S2:        0       down down        ?
S2:        1       down up          ?
S2:        2       up down          ?
S2:        3       up up            ?
S2: For each line: set SW9 SW8, move SW7 SW6 through down down, down up, up down, up up, and watch
S2: LEDG1 and LEDG0. The same (both on or both off) every time = yes. Different even once = no.
S2: ANSWER: raise the switch of every 'yes':  statement 0 = SW0,  1 = SW1,  2 = SW2,  3 = SW3.
S3: GOAL: where is YOUR statement (at the top)? Fill this table on paper from YOUR statement:
S3:    A B (SW7 SW6)    LEFT   RIGHT
S3:    0 0
S3:    0 1
S3:    1 0
S3:    1 1
S3: Now find the statement number whose LEDG1 (LEFT) and LEDG0 (RIGHT) show exactly your table.
S3: ANSWER: that number:   0 = all down   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0

[Q07] THEOREMS8 | Perfect induction: 8 statements of A B C | npub 8 | steps 4 | flat
B: Statement number = SW9 SW8 SW7 (HEX3: 0-7).  A = SW6, B = SW5, C = SW4 (HEX2 HEX1 HEX0).
B: LEFT side = LEDG1, RIGHT side = LEDG0.  Answer on SW3..SW0.
P0: Your statement for the last step:  A(A + B) = A
P1: Your statement for the last step:  BC + BC' = B
P2: Your statement for the last step:  AB + A'C + BC = AB + A'C
P3: Your statement for the last step:  (AB)' = A' + B'
P4: Your statement for the last step:  (A + B)' = A' + B'
P5: Your statement for the last step:  A + BC = (A + B)(A + C)
P6: Your statement for the last step:  A + BC = (A + B)C
P7: Your statement for the last step:  A + A'B = A + B
S1: WHAT YOU DO: check if statement 0 is TRUE. Each statement is LEFT = RIGHT:
S1: LEDG1 shows its LEFT side, LEDG0 its RIGHT side.
S1: 1. Put SW9, SW8, SW7 DOWN (= statement 0). Do not touch them.
S1: 2. Go over the 8 positions of A B C:
S1:    SW6 SW5 SW4 = down down down,  down down up,  down up down,  down up up,
S1:                  up down down,    up down up,    up up down,    up up up
S1: 3. In each position: are LEDG1 and LEDG0 the SAME (both on, or both off)?
S1: ANSWER: the same in all 8 positions -> SW0 UP (true).   Different even once -> SW0 DOWN (false).
S2: WHAT YOU DO: the same check for all 8 statements, and count how many are true.
S2: 1. Set the statement number on SW9 SW8 SW7:
S2:    statement 0 = SW9 SW8 SW7 down down down    1 = down down up    2 = down up down    3 = down up up
S2:              4 = up down down                  5 = up down up      6 = up up down      7 = up up up
S2: 2. For each statement do the 8 positions of A B C, as in step 1, and write: true / false.
S2: ANSWER: how many statements are true? Put the number:
S2:    0 = all down   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S3: WHAT YOU DO: find where YOUR statement (at the top of the screen) is on the board.
S3: 1. On paper, fill this table for YOUR statement - what its LEFT side gives, and what its RIGHT side gives:
S3:    A B C  (SW6 SW5 SW4)    LEFT   RIGHT
S3:    0 0 0
S3:    0 0 1
S3:    0 1 0
S3:    0 1 1
S3:    1 0 0
S3:    1 0 1
S3:    1 1 0
S3:    1 1 1
S3: 2. On the board, try statement numbers (SW9 SW8 SW7, as in step 2). For each one compare LEDG1 with
S3:    your LEFT column and LEDG0 with your RIGHT column, in the 8 positions of SW6 SW5 SW4.
S3: 3. The statement where BOTH lights match your table in all 8 positions is yours.
S3: ANSWER: its number:
S3:    0 = all down   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0

[Q08] MINSOP | The minimal sum of products | npub 1 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  F = LEDG0 (green).  Answer on SW3..SW0.
S1: GOAL: the truth table of F. Copy it to paper, go over the 8 rows once (0 = down, 1 = up), write F (LEDG0):
S1:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    Y
S1:    0 0 0
S1:    0 0 1
S1:    0 1 0
S1:    0 1 1
S1:    1 0 0
S1:    1 0 1
S1:    1 1 0
S1:    1 1 1
S1: ANSWER: how many 1s in the F column?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S2: GOAL: the minimal SOP. Write F as SIGMA of its minterms, then join minterms that differ in one letter
S2: (T10: XY + XY' = X), until no more joins - the fewest terms, each with the fewest letters.
S2: ANSWER: how many TERMS (products) does it have?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S3: GOAL: count the letters. In your minimal SOP, count every letter of every term (A'B + C = 3 letters).
S3: ANSWER: how many LITERALS?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0

[Q09] LITERAL | The hidden literal | npub 6 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  Y = LEDG0 (green).  Answer on SW3..SW0.
P0: Your expression:   Y = (A + B)(A' + ?) + BC      - one literal is hidden: ? is A, A', B, B', C or C'.
P1: Your expression:   Y = A'B + ?C + A'BC'      - one literal is hidden: ? is A, A', B, B', C or C'.
P2: Your expression:   Y = (AB + C)? + A'B'      - one literal is hidden: ? is A, A', B, B', C or C'.
P3: Your expression:   Y = A'? + BC' + AB'C      - one literal is hidden: ? is A, A', B, B', C or C'.
P4: Your expression:   Y = (A + ?)(B' + C) + A'BC'      - one literal is hidden: ? is A, A', B, B', C or C'.
P5: Your expression:   Y = AB + A'? + B'C'      - one literal is hidden: ? is A, A', B, B', C or C'.
S1: GOAL: the truth table of the board's Y. Copy it to paper, go over the 8 rows once, write Y (LEDG0):
S1:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    Y
S1:    0 0 0
S1:    0 0 1
S1:    0 1 0
S1:    0 1 1
S1:    1 0 0
S1:    1 0 1
S1:    1 1 0
S1:    1 1 1
S1: ANSWER: how many 1s?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S2: GOAL: find the hidden literal. Try ? = A in your expression: work out its table on paper and compare with
S2: the board's table. Not the same? Try A', then B, B', C, C' - only one of them matches.
S2: ANSWER:   A = SW0   A' = SW1   B = SW1+SW0   B' = SW2   C = SW2+SW0   C' = SW2+SW1
S3: GOAL: simplify Y (with the right literal) to a minimal SOP and count its letters (A'B + C = 3).
S3: ANSWER: how many LITERALS?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0

[Q10] STORY | From a story to an equation | npub 6 | steps 4 | flat
B: Your three letters are on SW9 SW8 SW7, in the order shown below (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  4 students' circuits = LEDG3..LEDG0.
B: Answer on SW3..SW0.
P0: You go to the Park (P) if it is NOT Raining (R) and you have Sandwiches (S) or Drinks (D).
P0: Letters:  R = SW9,  S = SW8,  D = SW7
P1: The alarm (Y) rings when the Door (D) is open and the system is Armed (A), or when there is Smoke (S).
P1: Letters:  D = SW9,  A = SW8,  S = SW7
P2: The light (L) is on when it is Dark (D) and someone Moves (M) - but never when the Battery (B) is low.
P2: Letters:  D = SW9,  M = SW8,  B = SW7
P3: You Enter (E) with a Hat (H) and Shoes (S), or with a Hat and no Shoes (S').
P3: Letters:  H = SW9,  S = SW8   (SW7 is not used)
P4: The fan (F) runs when it is Hot (H) and the window is not Open (O), or when a Kid (K) presses the button.
P4: Letters:  H = SW9,  O = SW8,  K = SW7
P5: You Win (W) if you get a Million (M) or a Notepad (N) - but only if you Play (P).
P5: Letters:  M = SW9,  N = SW8,  P = SW7
S1: GOAL: meet the 4 circuits. First write the story as an equation, on paper.
S1: Put all three letters to 1 (SW9, SW8, SW7 up).
S1: ANSWER: copy the lights - SWi up if LEDGi is on (SW3..SW0).
S2: GOAL: use YOUR equation. What is it when the letters are 1, 0, 1 (SW9 up, SW8 down, SW7 up)?
S2: Work it out on paper, from the equation.
S2: ANSWER: SW0 up if your equation gives 1, SW0 down if it gives 0.
S3: GOAL: which circuit is your equation? Fill this table from your equation (paper), then compare it
S3: with each light on the board, row by row:
S3:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    Y
S3:    0 0 0
S3:    0 0 1
S3:    0 1 0
S3:    0 1 1
S3:    1 0 0
S3:    1 0 1
S3:    1 1 0
S3:    1 1 1
S3: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for the light that matches in all 8 rows.

[Q11] DEMORGAN | De Morgan: which answer is right? | npub 6 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  4 students' answers = LEDG3..LEDG0.  Answer on SW3..SW0.
P0: Your expression:   Y = ((A + B')C)'
P1: Your expression:   Y = (A'B + C)'
P2: Your expression:   Y = (AB + C)'
P3: Your expression:   Y = ((A + B)C')'
P4: Your expression:   Y = (A + B + C)'
P5: Your expression:   Y = (A(B + C'))'
S1: GOAL: De Morgan on paper. Remove the outer bar of your Y (outside in: (XY)' = X' + Y', (X + Y)' = X'Y').
S1: Then fill the table of Y from your result:
S1:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    Y
S1:    0 0 0
S1:    0 0 1
S1:    0 1 0
S1:    0 1 1
S1:    1 0 0
S1:    1 0 1
S1:    1 1 0
S1:    1 1 1
S1: ANSWER: how many 1s in your Y column?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S2: GOAL: meet the 4 answers on the board. Put A B C = 0 0 0 (SW9, SW8, SW7 down).
S2: ANSWER: copy the lights - SWi up if LEDGi is on (SW3..SW0).
S3: GOAL: the right answer. Compare each light with your table, row by row (all 8 rows).
S3: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for the light that matches your Y in all 8 rows.

[Q12] ERRORS | Common errors: which simplifications are wrong? | npub 6 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  4 students' results = LEDG3..LEDG0.  Answer on SW3..SW0.
P0: Four students simplified your expression:   Y = A'BC + A'
P1: Four students simplified your expression:   Y = AB + AB'
P2: Four students simplified your expression:   Y = (A + BC)'
P3: Four students simplified your expression:   Y = (A + B)(A + C)
P4: Four students simplified your expression:   Y = AB + A'C + BC
P5: Four students simplified your expression:   Y = A + A'B
S1: GOAL: your own answer first. Work on YOUR expression (above) on paper, then fill its table:
S1:    row (SW9 SW8 SW7)    Y
S1:    0 0 0
S1:    0 0 1
S1:    0 1 0
S1:    0 1 1
S1:    1 0 0
S1:    1 0 1
S1:    1 1 0
S1:    1 1 1
S1: ANSWER: how many 1s in your Y column?   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1+SW0   4 = SW2   5 = SW2+SW0   6 = SW2+SW1   7 = SW2+SW1+SW0
S2: GOAL: meet the 4 results on the board. Put A B C = 0 0 0 (SW9, SW8, SW7 down).
S2: ANSWER: copy the lights - SWi up if LEDGi is on (SW3..SW0).
S3: GOAL: find the mistakes. Compare each light with your table, row by row (all 8 rows).

B: Select S1 = SW9, S0 = SW8.  Input C = SW7.  (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1)   Y = LEDG0 (green).   Your answer goes on SW3..SW0.

S1: GOAL: meet the mux. Put S1 S0 = 0 0 (SW9, SW8 down) - now Y shows D0.
S1: Look at Y with C = 0 (SW7 down), then with C = 1 (SW7 up).
S1: ANSWER: SW0 = Y with C = 0,   SW1 = Y with C = 1   (up = on).

S2: Look at Y with C = 0 (SW7 down) and with C = 1 (SW7 up):
S2:    Y 0 and 0 -> '0'     Y 1 and 1 -> '1'     Y = C (0 then 1) -> C     Y = opposite of C (1 then 0) -> C'
S2: ANSWER: '0' = all down    '1' = SW0    C = SW1    C' = SW1 + SW0
S3: GOAL: what is on D1? Put S1 S0 = 0 1 (SW9 down, SW8 up) - now Y shows D1.
S3: Look at Y with C = 0 (SW7 down) and with C = 1 (SW7 up):
S3:    Y 0 and 0 -> '0'     Y 1 and 1 -> '1'     Y = C (0 then 1) -> C     Y = opposite of C (1 then 0) -> C'
S3: ANSWER: '0' = all down    '1' = SW0    C = SW1    C' = SW1 + SW0
S4: GOAL: what is on D2? Put S1 S0 = 1 0 (SW9 up, SW8 down) - now Y shows D2.
S4: Look at Y with C = 0 (SW7 down) and with C = 1 (SW7 up):
S4:    Y 0 and 0 -> '0'     Y 1 and 1 -> '1'     Y = C (0 then 1) -> C     Y = opposite of C (1 then 0) -> C'
S4: ANSWER: '0' = all down    '1' = SW0    C = SW1    C' = SW1 + SW0
S5: GOAL: what is on D3? Put S1 S0 = 1 1 (SW9 up, SW8 up) - now Y shows D3.
S5: Look at Y with C = 0 (SW7 down) and with C = 1 (SW7 up):
S5:    Y 0 and 0 -> '0'     Y 1 and 1 -> '1'     Y = C (0 then 1) -> C     Y = opposite of C (1 then 0) -> C'
S5: ANSWER: '0' = all down    '1' = SW0    C = SW1    C' = SW1 + SW0

S4: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for the light LEDGi that is on.   Write it down: row 11 -> LEDG?

[Q20] PRIORITY | A priority circuit: who wins? | npub 1 | steps 5 | flat
B: Inputs A3 = SW9, A2 = SW8, A1 = SW7, A0 = SW6 (HEX3..HEX0).  Outputs Y3..Y0 = LEDG3..LEDG0.  Answer on SW3..SW0.
B: Yi = 1 when Ai is up and no STRONGER input is up. The order of strength is hidden.
S1: GOAL: meet the priority circuit. Raise ONLY SW9 (A3) - all of SW9..SW6 others down.
S1: One input alone always wins. Which light is on?
S1: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for the light LEDGi that is on.
S2: GOAL: two inputs together. Raise SW9 AND SW8 (A3 and A2). Only the stronger one lights its Y.
S2: Which light is on now?
S2: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for that light.
S3: GOAL: the STRONGEST input. Raise all four: SW9, SW8, SW7, SW6.
S3: The light that is on belongs to the strongest input.
S3: ANSWER: one switch up - SWi for that light.
S4: GOAL: the WEAKEST input - it wins only when it is alone.
S4: From all four up: lower the winner's switch, see who wins next, lower it too ... the last one is the weakest.
S4: ANSWER: one switch up for the weakest input:   A3 = SW3   A2 = SW2   A1 = SW1   A0 = SW0

S3: NOR: a letter that is 0 there is X, 1 there is X'.

[Q25] BUBBLES | Bubble pushing: which circuit is in the board? | npub 8 | steps 3 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7, D = SW6 (HEX3..HEX0).  Y = LEDG0 (green).  Answer on SW1 SW0.

P0: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P0:   0: n1 = NAND(D', A');  n2 = NAND(B, C');  Y = OR(n1, n2')
P0:   1: n1 = NAND(D, C);  n2 = NAND(C', B);  Y = NAND(n1', n2)
P0:   2: n1 = NOR(B, A');  n2 = NOR(C, B);  Y = OR(n1, n2)
P0:   3: n1 = NOR(A', B);  n2 = NOR(B', D');  Y = NAND(n1', n2)
P1: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P1:   0: n1 = NOR(C', B');  n2 = NOR(D, B);  Y = NAND(n1', n2)
P1:   1: n1 = NOR(B, D');  n2 = NAND(D', B');  Y = NOR(n1, n2')
P1:   2: n1 = NAND(C', B');  n2 = NOR(C', D');  Y = NOR(n1', n2)
P1:   3: n1 = NAND(D, A');  n2 = NOR(C', A');  Y = OR(n1', n2')
P2: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P2:   0: n1 = NOR(A, C');  n2 = NOR(D', A);  Y = NAND(n1', n2')
P2:   1: n1 = NAND(B', C);  n2 = NOR(A, B');  Y = NAND(n1', n2')
P2:   2: n1 = NOR(C, B);  n2 = NAND(A, D);  Y = NOR(n1', n2')
P2:   3: n1 = NAND(D, B);  n2 = NOR(B, C);  Y = AND(n1', n2')
P3: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P3:   0: n1 = NAND(C, A');  n2 = NAND(B, D');  Y = OR(n1', n2)
P3:   1: n1 = NOR(B', A);  n2 = NAND(D, C');  Y = NOR(n1, n2')
P3:   2: n1 = NAND(A, B');  n2 = NAND(C', A');  Y = OR(n1, n2')
P3:   3: n1 = NOR(A', C');  n2 = NAND(C', B);  Y = NOR(n1', n2')
P4: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P4:   0: n1 = NOR(B', A');  n2 = NOR(A, D);  Y = OR(n1, n2')
P4:   1: n1 = NAND(B, A);  n2 = NOR(B, C);  Y = OR(n1', n2')
P4:   2: n1 = NAND(C, B');  n2 = NAND(A, B);  Y = NAND(n1', n2)
P4:   3: n1 = NOR(D, C);  n2 = NAND(D', C');  Y = AND(n1, n2')
P5: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P5:   0: n1 = NAND(C, B);  n2 = NOR(B', C');  Y = OR(n1', n2)
P5:   1: n1 = NAND(C, A);  n2 = NOR(B, D);  Y = NAND(n1', n2')
P5:   2: n1 = NAND(B, C);  n2 = NOR(B, C');  Y = OR(n1, n2)
P5:   3: n1 = NOR(C', B);  n2 = NOR(C, A);  Y = NAND(n1', n2)
P6: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P6:   0: n1 = NOR(C, A);  n2 = NAND(C', A');  Y = NOR(n1, n2')
P6:   1: n1 = NOR(B', A);  n2 = NAND(D, C);  Y = AND(n1', n2)
P6:   2: n1 = NAND(B', C);  n2 = NAND(D', B);  Y = AND(n1', n2)
P6:   3: n1 = NOR(D', B');  n2 = NOR(B', A);  Y = AND(n1', n2')
P7: The board holds ONE of these circuits:
P7:   0: n1 = NOR(C', D');  n2 = NOR(C', D');  Y = AND(n1', n2')
P7:   1: n1 = NAND(D, B);  n2 = NOR(D, C);  Y = NOR(n1', n2')
P7:   2: n1 = NAND(B', D');  n2 = NOR(B', D');  Y = OR(n1', n2')
P7:   3: n1 = NOR(D', C);  n2 = NOR(B', D');  Y = NOR(n1, n2)
S1: GOAL: two quick looks at the board. Put A B C D = 0 0 0 0 (all down), then 1 1 1 1 (all up).
S1: ANSWER: SW0 = Y (LEDG0) at 0000,   SW1 = Y at 1111   (up = on).
S2: GOAL: which circuit? Push the bubbles of each circuit above to an SOP (paper), or just work out
S2: its Y in a few rows (start with 0000 and 1111). Compare with the board until only one circuit fits.
S2: ANSWER: its number:   0 = both down   1 = SW0   2 = SW1   3 = SW1 + SW0

[Q26] NANDNOR3 | Two-level logic: three gates, NAND or NOR each | npub 1 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8, C = SW7 (HEX3 HEX2 HEX1).  First level: n1 = LEDG3, n2 = LEDG2, n3 = LEDG1 (2-input NAND or NOR
B: of letters or their NOTs).  Second level: Y = LEDG0 = a 3-input NAND or NOR of n1, n2, n3.  Answer on SW3..SW0.
S1: GOAL: meet the circuit. Put A B C = 0 0 0 (SW9, SW8, SW7 down).
S1: ANSWER: copy the lights - SW3 = n1 (LEDG3), SW2 = n2, SW1 = n3, SW0 = Y (LEDG0).
S2: GOAL: n1 (LEDG3): NAND or NOR? Go over the 8 rows.
S2: A 2-input NAND is OFF in only 2 rows (both inputs 1).  A 2-input NOR is ON in only 2 rows (both inputs 0).
S2: ANSWER: SW0 up if n1 is a NAND, SW0 down if it is a NOR.
S3: GOAL: every gate. n2 and n3 the same way. For Y (3 inputs n1 n2 n3): watch a row where n1, n2, n3 are
S3: NOT all equal - a NAND gives 1 there, a NOR gives 0.
S3: ANSWER: SW3 = n1,  SW2 = n2,  SW1 = n3,  SW0 = Y:   up = NAND,  down = NOR.

S2: and compare with the board, until only one circuit is left.

[Q28] LATCH | A box with memory: what turns it on, what turns it off? | npub 1 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8 (HEX3 HEX2).  The box = LEDG0 (green).  Answer on SW1 SW0.
B: Move ONE switch at a time - two at once pass through a row in between.
S1: GOAL: meet the box. Start at A B = 0 0, then ONE switch at a time: SW8 up (01), SW9 up (11),
S1: SW8 down (10), SW9 down (00). Watch LEDG0 the whole time.
S1: ANSWER: SW0 up if LEDG0 changed at least once on the way.
S2: GOAL: the row that turns the box ON. The box stays as it is in most rows - only ONE row switches it on.
S2: Find it: when the light goes on, which row are you in?
S2: ANSWER: that row A B on SW1 SW0:   00 = both down   01 = SW0   10 = SW1   11 = SW1 + SW0
S3: GOAL: the row that turns the box OFF. (In the other two rows the box just remembers.)
S3: ANSWER: that row A B on SW1 SW0:   00 = both down   01 = SW0   10 = SW1   11 = SW1 + SW0

[Q29] DLATCH | A D latch: which input is the enable? | npub 1 | steps 4 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8 (HEX3 HEX2).  The box = LEDG0 (green).  Answer on SW1 SW0.
B: Move ONE switch at a time - two at once pass through a row in between.
S1: GOAL: a D latch: when its ENABLE is active it copies its DATA input, otherwise it remembers.
S1: One of A, B is the enable, the other is the data. Walk 00 -> 01 -> 11 -> 10 -> 00 (one switch at a time).
S1: ANSWER: SW0 up if LEDG0 changed at least once on the way.
S2: GOAL: which input is the ENABLE? Set one input, then move the OTHER one up and down and watch the box.
S2: The enable is the input that, in one of its positions, makes the box FOLLOW the other one; in its other position the box stays.
S2: ANSWER: SW1 up if A (SW9) is the enable,  SW0 up if B (SW8) is the enable - one switch.
S3: GOAL: is the enable active when it is 1 (up) or when it is 0 (down)?
S3: ANSWER: SW0 up if the box follows the data while the enable is UP,  SW0 down if while it is DOWN.

[Q30] SEQ | Combinational or sequential? (8 boxes) | npub 1 | steps 5 | flat
B: A = SW9, B = SW8 (HEX3 HEX2).  Box i = LEDGi (8 boxes, all get the same A and B).  Answer on SW7..SW0.
B: Move ONE switch at a time - two at once pass through a row in between.
S1: GOAL: read ONE box. Box 0 = LEDG0 (it has no memory).
S1: Try the four rows of A B (SW9 SW8) and write LEDG0 for each row.
S1: ANSWER: SW3 = LEDG0 at A B = 11,  SW2 = at 10,  SW1 = at 01,  SW0 = at 00.
S2: GOAL: a box that REMEMBERS. Box 1 = LEDG1.
S2: 1. A B = 00. Raise SW8, then lower it (back to 00). Write LEDG1.
S2: 2. Raise SW9, then lower it (back to 00). Write LEDG1.
S2: Both times A B = 00 - but LEDG1 is different: the box remembers what came before.
S2: ANSWER: SW1 = LEDG1 after move 1,  SW0 = LEDG1 after move 2.
S3: GOAL: which other boxes remember? Test all 8 on two long paths, one switch at a time:
S3: Path 1 from 00: SW8 up, SW9 up, SW8 down, SW9 down. Write LEDG7..LEDG0.
S3: Path 2 from 00: SW9 up, SW8 up, SW9 down, SW8 down. Write LEDG7..LEDG0.
S3: ANSWER: SWi up for every box whose light is different at the end of the two paths.
S4: GOAL: ALL boxes with memory. Some remember only in another row, not at 00.
S4: For every row of A B, arrive at it from both neighbours (one switch at a time)
S4: and watch whether a light depends on where you came from.
S4: ANSWER: SWi up for every box with memory (SW7..SW0).
